back: Materials and parts are delivered only as they are needed, so stock is kept to a minimum.
Large stocks are held as a safeguard against late deliveries, rising demand or price rises.
Lower storage and holding costs, less cash tied up, less waste, more space, quick response to change.
A late delivery stops production; needs reliable suppliers; frequent deliveries may cost more; little buffer for sudden demand.
EOQ = √(2DS ÷ H): D yearly demand, S cost per order, H yearly holding cost of one unit.
Total cost = (D ÷ Q) × S + (Q ÷ 2) × H. Average stock is half the order size.
Yearly ordering cost equals yearly holding cost, and total cost is at its lowest.
Constant demand, fixed ordering cost, constant holding cost, no discounts, no delivery delay.
JIT suits predictable demand and reliable nearby suppliers; JIC suits uncertain supply or demand.
